uncertainties: 271 Anatolia: Palmyra confirmed to have taken Galatia/Ancyra (CAP) and, by inference, Cilicia (CIL, contiguous with Syria); Bithynia (BIT) and coastal Ionia (ION) explicitly held out (Chalcedon siege failed), so kept Roman. Pontus (PON) and Cyprus (CYP) are genuinely uncertain and were conservatively kept Roman for lack of positive evidence.

271 Mesopotamia (MES_N/Osroene): assigned to Palmyra as a continuation of Odaenathus's earlier defence of the eastern frontier against Persia; sources do not confirm Zenobia's administrative control here as clearly as for Egypt/Syria/Anatolia, so this is a judgment call.

Armenia 252-287: Sassanid princes ruled occupied Armenia after Khosrov II's assassination in 252; Tiridates III restored with Roman military backing in 287 (Peace of Nisibis in 299 later formalized Roman support). The 271 slice therefore shows Armenia (ARM, ARM_W) under Sassanid control.

Armenia partition of 387: Rome received roughly the western third (Acilisene/Sophene, mapped here to ARM_W near Erzurum), Persia the larger eastern two-thirds (mapped to ARM, the Ararat/Yerevan core). The exact demarcation ran through Karin/Erzurum itself, so the ARM_W/ARM split is a simplification of a messier border.

Bosporan Kingdom's decline is poorly dated (last coinage 341; scholars disagree on exact end). Kept it nominally independent/client through 370, becoming a Hunnic-dominated territory (assigned to 'huns') only at 395, in line with sources describing it becoming a Hunnic vassal in the late 4th century.

Poland (POL_W, SIL, POL_C, POL_S) and the North European Plain are treated as a broad 'germani' culture zone throughout (Przeworsk-culture Vandal/Burgundian/Lugii groups); no distinct Vandal or Burgundian polity entity was created before this era's end (395), since their historically attested kingdoms only form in the 5th century (matching the data-spec's canonical founded dates).

Proto-Slavic ethnogenesis (Zarubintsy/Kyiv archaeological cultures in UKR_W/BLR, c.100 BCE-300 CE) is a real but contested strand; since the data-spec pins 'slavs_early' to the 500s CE, UKR_W was instead tracked as sarmatians (to 180) then goths (235-370, Chernyakhov culture) and BLR kept as balts_early throughout, deferring the Slavic question to the following era.

RUS_S (Chernigov & Upper Don) and RUS_NW/RUS_C are sparsely attested in this period; assigned to balts_early (RUS_S) and finnic_peoples (RUS_NW, RUS_C) as a reasonable default rather than precise attestation.

Netherlands (NED)/Frisia: treated as loosely Roman-aligned/tributary throughout rather than showing the 28 CE Frisian revolt and subsequent on-again-off-again control, since no slice year falls close enough to that event to justify a dedicated entity.

Population figures for tribal/culture entities (germani, balts_early, finnic_peoples, sami, sarmatians, goths, etc.) are rough order-of-magnitude estimates for the mapped regions only; no census data exists for this period and figures are extrapolated from general demographic literature on Iron Age/Migration Period Europe.

Roman Empire population at 395 split (west ~22M / east ~27M) follows commonly cited orders of magnitude but individual scholarly estimates vary considerably (Diocese-level figures are contested); treated as approximate.

Dacia's eastern reaches (WLC/Wallachia beyond the Limes Transalutanus, and MDA/Moldavia) are simplified: Roman Dacia (117-235) is shown covering all of TRN and WLC, though the eastern Limes Transalutanus zone was a looser military frontier rather than fully settled province territory.
